facts.statement: The genus Maxakalisaurus was discovered in 1998 in the Adamantina Formation of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
facts.quote: Maxakalisaurus is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur, found in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil, in the state of Minas Gerais in 1998.

facts.statement: Alexander W. A. Kellner and his team formally described Maxakalisaurus topai as a new genus and species in 2006.
facts.quote: In 2006, a team led by Alexander W. A. Kellner described the remains as a new genus and species of sauropod, Maxakalisaurus topai.

facts.statement: Excavations for the holotype skeleton took place between 1998 and 2002 along a road 45 km west of Prata, Minas Gerais.
facts.quote: Over the course of four field seasons, from 1998 to 2002, the National Museum of Brazil excavated a partial skeleton of a titanosaur along the Campina Verde - Prata road, 45 km to the west of Prata, Minas Gerais.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as MN 5013-V, was housed at the National Museum of Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype, MN 5013-V, was housed at the National Museum of Brazil.

facts.statement: Fossils recovered from the type locality include remains belonging to both an adult and a subadult individual.
facts.quote: Some of the elements from the type locality pertained to an adult individual and others pertained to a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Many elements of the holotype were destroyed in the National Museum of Brazil fire on September 2, 2018, though some survived.
facts.quote: Some elements of the holotype were lost in the National Museum of Brazil fire on 2 September 2018, but several elements survived the fire and were recovered.

facts.statement: The fossil belongs to the Baru Formation of the Late Cretaceous, dating to approximately 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil pertenece a la formación Baru del cretácico tardío hace unos 80 millones de años.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Maxakali tribe, while the species name refers to their deity Topa.
facts.quote: El nombre fue puesto en honor a la tribu Maxakali, y la especie M. topai a uno de sus dioses, Topa.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus is classified as a medium-sized titanosaur.
facts.quote: Maxakalisaurus is considered a medium-sized titanosaur.

facts.statement: The type specimen represents an animal approximately 12.1 meters long and weighing an estimated 5 tons.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Maxakalisaurus belonged to an animal about 12.1 m long, with an estimated weight of 5 t.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus possessed a long neck and tail, as well as ridged teeth, a feature unusual among sauropods.
facts.quote: It had a long neck and tail, ridged teeth (unusual among sauropods) and lived about 80 million years ago.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus had osteoderms, a trait shared by many other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Like many other titanosaurs, Maxakalisaurus had osteoderms.

facts.statement: The dinosaur had long neck and tail, and unusually grooved teeth among sauropods.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuello y cola largos, y cosa poco usual en los saurópodos dientes con surcos.

facts.statement: The discovered specimen is a juvenile estimated at 13 meters long and 9 tons, though adults may have reached 20 meters.
facts.quote: Es considerado unos de los dinosaurios más grandes encontrados en Brasil, el hallado es un ejemplar juvenil de unos 13 metros de largo y 9 toneladas de peso pero se estima que un adulto hubiera llegado a los 20 metros.

facts.statement: Specimen MN 5013-V was stored at the National Museum of Brazil in Rio de Janeiro before being destroyed in the 2018 fire.
facts.quote: Este espécimen MN 5013-V se guardaba en el Museo Nacional de Brasil, Río de Janeiro, en Brasil antes del incendio que lo destruyó el 2 de septiembre de 2018.

facts.statement: A new specimen containing a dentary and teeth was described as belonging to Maxakalisaurus in 2016.
facts.quote: En 2016, un nuevo espécimen que comprende un dentario y dientes fue descrito como perteneciente a Maxakalisaurus.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus lived in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: Maxakalisaurus is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur, found in the Adamantina Formation of Brazil, in the state of Minas Gerais in 1998.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus lived approximately 80 million years ago.
facts.quote: It had a long neck and tail, ridged teeth (unusual among sauropods) and lived about 80 million years ago.

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Maxakalisaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus is the genus name for this extinct animal.
facts.quote: genus: Maxakalisaurus

facts.statement: The specific species name is topai, making the full name Maxakalisaurus topai.
facts.quote: species: topai

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Saltasauridae

facts.statement: Maxakalisaurus belongs to the tribe Aeolosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Aeolosaurini

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Maxakalisaurus within Aeolosaurini alongside Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético recuperó a Maxakalisaurus como una Aelosaurínído junto con Aeolosaurus y Gondwanatitan.

facts.statement: South American sauropods, including Maxakalisaurus, evolved greater diversity and unusual traits due to a lack of significant competition.
facts.quote: Because sauropods seem to have lacked significant competition in South America, they evolved there with greater diversity and more unusual traits than elsewhere in the world.

facts.statement: Alexander Kellner stated that Maxakalisaurus is the largest dinosaur ever described in Brazil.
facts.quote: "Este es el dinosaurio más grande jamás descrito en Brasil", dijo Alexander Kellner, autor principal de la descripción científica.

facts.statement: Researchers have found bones that appear to belong to larger dinosaurs in Brazil, but these have not yet been assembled for scientific description.
facts.quote: "Hemos encontrado los huesos de lo que parecen ser dinosaurios más grandes, pero aún no hemos podido reunirlos para descripciones científicas".
